claims.text: The proposed intervention is to add approximately 2–5 wt% titanium to the boride during component synthesis.
The baseline components have a typical boride microstructure without a deliberate dopant or secondary-phase addition.
Titanium addition will promote in situ formation of a TiB2-rich interlayer during molten-aluminum exposure.
The TiB2-rich interlayer will be continuous and thin.
The TiB2-rich interlayer will form along grain boundaries and at the component surface.
Titanium reacts with boron in the boride matrix to form TiB2.
TiB2 is chemically inert under the proposed molten-aluminum exposure conditions.
TiB2 has a lattice compatible with the unspecified base boride.
The TiB2-rich phase will reduce wetting of the component by molten aluminum.
The TiB2-rich phase will reduce penetration of molten aluminum into the component.
Reduced aluminum wetting and penetration will lower the kinetics of corrosive attack.
Ti-alloyed boride components will have lower corrosion depth than unalloyed boride controls after molten-aluminum exposure.
Ti-alloyed boride components will have lower weight loss than unalloyed boride controls after molten-aluminum exposure.
The anticipated corrosion-resistance improvement is approximately 20%, although the precise value is uncertain.
The intervention is expected to remain beneficial at molten-aluminum temperatures of approximately 650–700 °C and for typical plating exposure durations.
The intervention may become less effective at temperatures significantly above 700 °C.
The intervention may become less effective during unusually long immersion times.
A controlled comparison at approximately 660 °C can test Ti-modified samples against otherwise comparable samples without Ti.
Corrosion depth, weight loss, and TiB2-layer formation and continuity can be evaluated using cross-sectional SEM, EDS mapping, and XRD.

The hypothesis will be rejected if Ti-bearing samples fail to show a statistically significant approximately 15–20% reduction in corrosion depth and weight loss, or if no continuous TiB2-rich interlayer is observed.
